result.title: Bits, Not Boxes: Label-Free Layer Selection for Visual Localization in VLMs
result.summary: Attention maps cheaply show where a vision-language model (VLM) looks, but attention sinks make them unreliable for localization. Contrasting the question with a generic prompt suppresses sinks, yet only some layers localize the queried object. Existing methods find these layers with box annotations or fixed rules. We show that attention itself can identify them. A question changes how much a head attends to the image and where this attention goes. The two effects separate exactly, and the second, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, indicates which layers localize. WhereBits turns these where-to-look bits into a layer prior and combines it with per-head contrastive scores. Its three design constants were fixed once on labeled COCO data, and a new model or resolution needs only unlabeled questions. Across eight VLMs, WhereBits matches the pointing accuracy of box-tuned layers on COCO and RefCOCO and ranks target tokens better. This advantage holds on a held-out model family and at higher resolutions. Its COCO pointing accuracy is 0.72, against 0.22 for mean attention. In training-free zoom-in, its crops raise V* accuracy by 6.0 points under forced-choice evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 WhereBits：用无标注问题上测量到的「where-to-look」比特量作为层先验，结合逐头对比分数，免框标注地挑出能定位被问物体的层；在八个 VLM、COCO/RefCOCO 定位与免训练 zoom-in 上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 VLM 内部视觉证据落在哪些层/头、以及注意力 sink 对定位的干扰，可供核查 LVR 中视觉旁路与证据读取的深度位置；但未触及 latent 推理状态生成，注意力定位是否等同于答案真正使用视觉内容仍需确认。
